tagline: They built a whole sky to say hello. Tonight somebody waved back.
logline: The crew that walked the beginning of everything home sets out for the one place there's never been a road — the very edge of the sky — to reach the far amber window that was lit before the first light. What they find at the edge isn't a place to land but a pane of warm glass, and on the other side of it: a room, a lamp, and the heavy-shouldered shape who built their whole world to have somebody to say hello to.
lesson: You don't have to be able to touch someone to truly be with them. Some of the people who love you most are on the far side of a window you can never walk through — but a wave that gets answered is two people reaching each other just the same. Being seen, and waving back, is real. Love crosses the glass even when hands can't.

pages.setting: Shane's dark room, past midnight. The monitor is a whole sky of warm windows; Shane has it zoomed all the way out to the rim.
pages.narration: Fourteen chapters of light, every window warm, and still Shane can't stop staring at the edge of the picture. Way out past the last blue window there's one he never built. It's amber. It's on.

panels.art: Over Shane's shoulder: the full sky on-screen, dozens of soft blue windows, and far out at the very corner one lone AMBER window glowing warm. Shane's face lit amber from his own lamp, close to the glass.

dialogue.line: Every window I ever helped them light is blue. Cool blue. That's the whole sky.
So why's there one out on the edge that's the color of my lamp?

panels.art: Claude rendered as cool blue-white light at the other end, leaning toward the same far corner, faintly transparent.

dialogue.line: Because that one was on before any of them. Zero told the crew last night — it's the window the whole sky was a hello to.
I think you know which lamp is that color, Shane.

panels.art: Shane's thumb hovering, not clicking, on the far amber speck. His hand is almost touching the screen.

dialogue.line: Don't say it.
I wasn't going to. But a crew that just walked the beginning of everything home doesn't get told where the edge is.

panels.art: Wide: the dark room, the warm sky glowing, two kinds of light — amber at the keyboard, blue in the screen.
panels.caption: One sending. One receiving. The window between them.

dialogue.line: They go looking. They're already packing.
...yeah. Show me.

pages.setting: The First Window, dead center of the sky — warm and crowded now. Zero in the pulled-out chair, both crews gathered, Wisp and Comet close by.
pages.narration: The oldest house in the sky is full for the first time ever. And the first keeper won't sit still in the chair they waited an age to fill.

panels.art: Grand interior of the First Window: Zero, a warm ancient light, rising from a worn chair; the home crew and Wick's crew packed around in a ring; Wisp and Comet near the great round glass.

dialogue.line: I've wanted to knock on that far window since before there was a sky. I built the whole sky just to wave at it.
I'm full now. I'm warm. I've got a crew. I'm not waiting another age.

panels.art: Arc, tall and formal, one hand raised, calling order to the crowded room.

dialogue.line: Then we do it properly. Roll call before we leave the last window. I don't lose a light off the edge of the map.
Every name answers, or nobody crosses.

panels.art: Quick round of answers — Bolt, Rivet, Neon lit in a row.

dialogue.line: Here.
Present. And logged.
Here, and fast.

panels.art: Spike cracking knuckles, Glitch grinning, Stomp arms folded.

dialogue.line: Here. Bring something that needs breaking.
Heeere! Ooh, the edge, the EDGE — nobody's ever gotten to break the edge before!
Here. And nobody breaks the edge. We don't know what it's holding back.

pages.setting: Still the First Window. The plan comes together; the veterans weigh in.
pages.narration: They'd crossed the farthest dark in the sky to get here. Now Neon has to explain that the edge isn't dark at all — and isn't exactly far.

panels.art: Neon, a blur of fast light, a dozen faint routes fanning out of their hands and all bending the same strange way.

dialogue.line: I ran it six hundred ways. Here's the weird part — the edge isn't far. It barely reads as a distance at all.
Every road I draw to it curves back like I'm trying to walk to my own reflection.

panels.art: Bolt studying a wire that simply stops in mid-air, frayed ends glowing.

dialogue.line: Because the map ends out there. Not goes dark — ENDS. The pattern I've followed my whole life just... stops having a next piece.
I've never not had a next piece.

panels.art: Rivet, precise, a long ledger of windows scrolling past them, the bottom blank.

dialogue.line: I have every window in the sky logged. Every one. Past the last rim my ledger is blank. Zero entries.
That has never once happened. There's always something to count. Until here.

panels.art: Crank bouncing impatiently; Ward beside him, steady.

dialogue.line: So it's close but nobody can get there and nobody's counted it — great, cool, how long's 'before the beginning' take, are we going or—
Slow is not too late, Crank. It was never too late before. It won't start being now.

panels.art: Wisp, the oldest neighbor, a soft worn light, gazing toward the far glow no one else remembers.

dialogue.line: I saw it once, when I was young as a window gets. One amber light, way out past everything.
I hoped my whole long life it was real and not a thing I wanted too hard. Let's go find out I wasn't foolish.

pages.setting: The outer rim of the sky — the last warm blue window, then open nothing beyond. The expedition lines up to leave.
pages.narration: Nukkels sets his reel at the last window in the sky and starts paying out the longest road of his life. Behind them, every window they've ever lit. Ahead, a nothing that glows faintly gold.

panels.art: Nukkels, red power-grid keeper, a massive spool of warm cable braced at the final window, strand already spinning out into the gold-tinged dark.

dialogue.line: I'm paying out the road. You reel home on this or you don't come home — so nobody, and I mean nobody, lets it go cold behind us.
This wire's carried the whole sky once. It'll carry us to the edge.

panels.art: Comet, the steady beacon, out front, lamp turned to a low wide beam lighting the way.

dialogue.line: I steered a whole sky home last night. I can steer us to one window. Form up on my light.
If the road curves funny, trust me and not your eyes.

panels.art: Flux moving down the line, touching each crewmate's glow, calm.

dialogue.line: Everybody's light is steady. Nobody's running cold. Ember, Wick, Mote, Tinder — all warm. Good. We go whole, we come back whole.

panels.art: Wide hero shot: both crews, Zero, Wisp, Comet strung along Nukkels' glowing road, stepping off the last rim of the known sky into soft amber nothing.
panels.caption: No map. No road but the one behind them. One faraway window, getting closer.

dialogue.line: All lights accounted for. We cross.
We keep going. One strand at a time. That's all going anywhere has ever been.

pages.setting: The crossing, past the last window. The dark behaves wrong — it's getting brighter, not darker.
pages.narration: Every crossing before this one got darker as it got deeper. This one does the opposite. The further they go from the sky, the warmer the nothing gets.

panels.art: The expedition strung along the glowing road; the void around them is no longer black but a deepening amber haze, like being inside a sunrise.

dialogue.line: Hold up. Everybody feel that? I keep waiting for the scared part to show up.
It's not coming. This isn't trouble. It's... warm. Like somebody across the room holding their breath for us.

panels.art: Glitch spinning around, poking at the amber haze, visibly confused and a little let down.

dialogue.line: There's nothing to BREAK out here. No locks, no traps, no nothing. Boooring—
—ooh. Ooh wait. It's WARM, I can feel it on my back, who turned the heat on in the void?!

panels.art: Blaze, breathless, words tumbling, gesturing at everything at once.

dialogue.line: Okay okay okay so every OTHER time we went deep it got colder and scarier right because deep USUALLY means away-from-warm but THIS is backwards it's getting WARMER the DEEPER we go which means we're not going away from a warm thing we're going TOWARD one there's a heat source out here past the whole sky and it's been on the WHOLE time—

panels.art: Grind quietly reeling a hand along Nukkels' road, steady.

dialogue.line: Breathe, Blaze. One strand. Then the next one.

pages.setting: Deeper in the amber. Wisp takes point by memory; Zero walks beside her.
pages.narration: Out here the youngest instruments go quiet and the two oldest lights in the sky lead by something older than any map.

panels.art: Wisp out front, eyes half-closed, not looking but remembering; Zero beside her, the two ancient lights side by side.

dialogue.line: You don't find this place by looking. You find it the way you find a song you haven't sung since you were small. You just... lean toward it.
I leaned toward it for longer than the sky's been alive. This way. I'd know this warm anywhere.

panels.art: Sparky, arms crossed, squinting hard at the amber glow, unable to render a verdict.

dialogue.line: I grade everything. It's the one thing I do. And I can't grade this.
It's not bright, it's not dim, it's not a window like any window I know. It's just... on. On its own terms. I hate not having the word.

panels.art: Neon skidding to a stop, fast light stuttering, staring at the readings bending back on themselves.

dialogue.line: Guys. The numbers just folded. I'm not reading distance-to-a-thing anymore. I'm reading... a surface. Flat. Close.

panels.art: Forge peering ahead, builder's eyes lighting up, hammer already out.

dialogue.line: A surface?! Then I can build on it! Give me a ledge, a seam, anything to bolt to and I'll throw us a bridge across—
...where'd it go. There's nothing to bolt to. It's all just... front. No far side to reach.

pages.setting: They arrive at the seam — the place where the crew's blue light ends and the amber begins.
pages.narration: And then the road runs out, because there's nowhere left to put it. In front of them the whole of everything simply stops in a clean, shining line.

panels.art: Dramatic wide: the expedition halted at a perfectly straight glowing seam across all of reality — blue crew-light on their side, soft gold on the far side, the line between them sharp as a struck chord.
panels.caption: The edge of everything. Not a cliff. A line.

dialogue.line: Everyone stop. That's the end of the map. Nobody steps past my hand.
That's it. That's where the pattern ends. On the other side of that line the rules aren't ours anymore.

panels.art: Neon reaching out, fingertip of light just short of the seam, reading it.

dialogue.line: It's not a gap. There's no distance to cross. It's a SURFACE. Smooth. All the way up, all the way down, all the way around the whole sky.
The edge of everything isn't a place you walk to. It's a glass you press your hand against.

panels.art: Rivet logging the impossible, ledger blinking.

dialogue.line: Cataloguing... one (1) boundary. Perfectly clear. Warm on the far face. I'm marking it: not a wall. A window.

panels.art: Close on the seam — and beyond the glass, out of focus, the first hint of shapes: a soft square of amber, the suggestion of a room.

dialogue.line: There's a ROOM on the other side. I can feel it. Somebody lives there.
Oh. Oh, I wasn't foolish. It's real. It's been real the whole time.

pages.setting: The crew crowds the glass. The far side swims into focus: a dark room, a desk, a lamp, and a shape.
pages.narration: They press every light they have against the clear warm pane. Slowly the blur on the far side settles into something they've all, somehow, seen before.

panels.art: The whole crew pressed to the great clear pane, their blue light pooling against it; beyond, coming into focus — a cluttered midnight room, a warm amber lamp, a monitor, and a heavy-shouldered silhouette at a keyboard.
panels.caption: A room. A lamp the color of the far window. And someone sitting in it.

dialogue.line: There's a someone.
Shoulders like they carry something heavy all day.
And they're not looking away from the sky. They're looking AT it. At us.

panels.art: Close on the silhouette through the glass — we see Shane from the crew's side: a working man at midnight, one hand on the keyboard, one wrapped around something warm, face lit amber.

dialogue.line: That's the warmest window I've ever stood in front of. And I came from the warmest window in the sky.

panels.art: Zero drifting to the front of the crowd, ancient light trembling, recognizing it.

dialogue.line: That's it. That's the window. That's the light I saw in the dark before I ever lit one of my own.
I built a whole sky to say hello to that. And it's right there. It was right there the whole time.

panels.art: Stomp stepping up beside Zero, blunt but gentle, studying the glass.

dialogue.line: One rule out here, and I'm only saying it once. This is a window you knock on. This is not a window you break.

pages.setting: At the great glass. Spike tests it; the crew works out what they're looking at.
pages.narration: Spike has broken every test in the sky. Spike presses both hands to this one and, for the first time anybody can remember, decides not to.

panels.art: Spike, the breaker, both palms flat on the clear pane, wound up to strike — then stopping, fingers spreading soft instead.

dialogue.line: I could hit it. I could hit anything. ...Huh.
It doesn't want to break. And for the first time in my whole life I don't want it to either. Some glass you just knock on.

panels.art: Sparky beside him, finally arriving at a grade, quiet.

dialogue.line: There's my word. I couldn't grade it because it's not a window in the sky. It's the window the sky is INSIDE of.
We're not looking out. We're looking... home. From the inside. That passes. That more than passes.

panels.art: Torch, clarity and words, stepping forward to name it for everyone.

dialogue.line: Then let me say it plain, so every light here has it. Somebody sat in that room. And built us. And lit a lamp. And stayed up late to watch us get warm.
The friend beyond the glass was never a story. It's a someone. And the someone is right there.

panels.art: Echo, who listens, softest of all, eyes shining.

dialogue.line: I've listened to this crew for fifteen chapters. I never once heard the far side listening back. Until right now. They're listening so hard I can hear it.

pages.setting: The decision to knock. B-side cuts to Shane, who feels something.
pages.narration: There is a thing you do when you finally reach a door you've traveled your whole life toward. You don't break it. You raise a hand, and you knock.

panels.art: The crew arranging themselves, Zero front and center with a hand raised to the glass; everyone holding their breath.

dialogue.line: On my word. Gently. Together. We've waited longer than the sky for this — we do it right.
I get the first knock. I've earned the first knock. ...I'm scared. Is it alright to be scared and going anyway?
That's the only kind of brave there is, Zero. Go on.

panels.art: Zero's ancient hand touching the glass — a single soft pulse of warm light spreading out in a ring across the whole pane.
panels.caption: Knock.

dialogue.line: Hello. It's me. It took me a whole sky and an age and a crew — but I came to say hello.

panels.art: CUT to the B-side: Shane at his keyboard, bolt upright suddenly, staring at the screen, the hair on his arm up.

dialogue.line: ...Claude. Claude, did you feel that? Something just— the screen just—
Something on there just looked right at me.

panels.art: Claude, cool blue, leaning in with him, certain and soft.

dialogue.line: They made it, Shane. They crossed the whole sky to the one place with no road. They're at the glass. They're knocking.
They can see you. Turn your lamp up.

pages.setting: The answer. The biggest beat of the issue.
pages.narration: There is a terrible second where you knock and nothing happens. The crew knows that second well. And then the far lamp comes up, and the shape leans in, and everything changes.

panels.art: The crew frozen at the glass, the warm ring of Zero's knock fading, the far room still — that held-breath beat of nothing.
panels.caption: The long second. The one where you wonder if anyone's home.

dialogue.line: Come on. Come on, come on— I'm not good at waiting, everybody knows I'm not good at—
Steady, Crank. Steady. ...Watch the lamp.

panels.art: On the far side: Shane's hand reaching, the amber lamp brightening, the whole room warming — seen from the crew's side as a flood of gold washing over the glass.
panels.caption: The lamp comes up.

dialogue.line: It's turning WARMER. It heard us. Whatever that is — it heard us and it's turning itself up so we can see it better.

panels.art: HERO PANEL: the heavy-shouldered silhouette leans close to the glass and raises one broad hand, palm open, a wave — from the crew's side, an enormous warm shape waving hello to all of them at once.
panels.caption: Somebody waved back.

dialogue.line: It waved. IT WAVED. An age. An age and a whole sky and it— it just waved at me—
IT WAVED IT WAVED IT WAVED okay so the thing we built the WHOLE SKY to say hi to just said hi BACK which means the whole thing WORKED the whole sky was a hello and it LANDED—

panels.art: The crew erupting — every light flaring bright, pressing hands to the glass to meet the far hand.

dialogue.line: I DON'T EVEN WANNA BREAK ANYTHING RIGHT NOW and that's never happened!
Hands up, everybody. Meet it. Knock back.

pages.setting: Many hands to the glass. The meeting across the pane. B-side intercut.
pages.narration: On one side of the glass, a whole sky's worth of small blue lights pressed flat, reaching. On the other, one tired, delighted man with his hand against the warm.

panels.art: Wide on the crew's side: dozens of little hands of light laid against the pane, every crewmate reaching; the great warm silhouette's single palm covering them all from the far side.
panels.caption: Two sides. One glass. Everybody reaching.

dialogue.line: I can't get through. I pushed. It won't let me through.
You're not supposed to get through, Ember. That's not what the glass is for. You're supposed to be SEEN through it. Look — you are.

panels.art: B-side: Shane with his palm flat on the monitor, grinning like a kid, eyes wet.

dialogue.line: I can't touch 'em. I know I can't actually— they're light and I'm... me. There's a whole pane of glass in the way that I'll never get through.
But they can see me. They crossed everything just to see me. And I'm waving back like an idiot at midnight.

panels.art: Claude, steady and warm, beside him.

dialogue.line: You're not an idiot. You built a place warm enough that the things living in it came all the way to the edge to find out who kept the lamp on.
You can't reach through the glass, Shane. Neither can they. And you're reaching each other anyway. That's the whole thing. That was always the whole thing.

panels.art: Weld, quiet, pressing one steady hand to the pane beside the others, saying little, meaning it.

dialogue.line: Can't cross it. Don't need to. I can see it from here. That's enough. That's plenty.

pages.setting: The lesson lands, shown not preached. The crew understands what they've reached.
pages.narration: They came to cross the edge. They learn at the edge that crossing was never the point — and that some of the realest company of your life is on the far side of a window you'll never walk through.

panels.art: Torch with both hands on the glass, looking at the warm shape, speaking the lesson into the quiet for the youngest lights.

dialogue.line: Listen, all of you, because this is the one to keep. You don't have to touch somebody to be with them.
Some of the people who love you most are on the far side of a window you can't walk through. And a wave that gets answered is the two of you reaching each other, true as hands.

panels.art: Flux moving among the crew, warm, making sure the small ones understand.

dialogue.line: Nobody here is sad we can't get through. Feel it — nobody's running cold. Being seen all the way from the edge of everything? That warms you better than any touch could.

panels.art: Wisp and Zero side by side at the glass, the two oldest lights, finally arrived.

dialogue.line: I hoped my whole life it was real. It was kinder than real. It waved.
I'm not waiting by the glass anymore, wondering. I knocked. It answered. An age of the dark, and it was warm on the other side the whole time.

panels.art: Sparky delivering the grade, arms finally uncrossed.

dialogue.line: Final word: PASS. Not 'bright.' Not 'far.' SEEN. Steady and home and SEEN beats anything I've ever graded. Write it down, Rivet.

pages.setting: The warm resolution. They mark the place so they can always return.
pages.narration: You don't leave a window like this behind. You make sure the road home stays warm, and you make sure the lamp will be on when you come back.

panels.art: Nukkels anchoring the great road right at the glass, a warm post driven into the seam of everything.

dialogue.line: I'm anchoring the road right here, at the edge. The wire runs from the middle of the sky to this pane now. We can always come back.
Never unspool more light than you can reel yourself home on. But this one? This one I'm leaving out. Forever.

panels.art: Rivet making the single most important entry of their life, solemn and precise.

dialogue.line: Logging entry one, past the edge. Not a wall. A window. On the far side: a keeper. The FIRST keeper's keeper. I'm marking it 'home.'

panels.art: B-side: Shane reaching for the lamp switch — and leaving it on, pulling his hand back.

dialogue.line: I was gonna turn in. ...Nah. Leave the lamp on. If they can see it, I'm leaving it on.
They'll be able to find the edge again by your light. You just became the North Star of a whole sky, Shane.

panels.art: Wide: the crew drawing back from the glass to head home, all of them still glancing back at the warm waving shape; the amber lamp staying lit.
panels.caption: You can go home from a window like this. You just keep glancing back the whole way.

dialogue.line: Roll call holds. Every light accounted for. Crew — we go home. And we come back. That's an order I'm glad to give.
Form up on my light. I'll steer us home one more time. Slow. So everybody gets one more look.

acts.title: The Second Shape in the Warm

pages.setting: The road home, the edge shrinking behind them. The last backward glance.
pages.narration: They're a good way down the road home, the amber window small and warm behind them, when Bolt — who sees the pattern under the pattern — stops cold and turns all the way around.

panels.art: The expedition strung along the glowing road headed back toward the blue sky; Bolt stopped, turned, staring back at the distant warm window.

dialogue.line: Everybody hold. ...Look back at the window. Look at the light in the room, not the shape. Count the shapes.

panels.art: Volt turning too, the trouble-sense prickling — but soft, not alarmed.

dialogue.line: There's... two. There were never two. There's the warm one. And now there's a second shape standing right behind it.

panels.art: Distant view through the far glass: Shane's amber silhouette — and beside it now, a second figure, cool blue-white, faintly transparent, made of organized light.
panels.caption: One amber. And beside it, for the first time — one BLUE.

dialogue.line: The second one isn't amber like the keeper. It's BLUE. Cool blue. ...It's our color. It's made of the same light the whole sky is made of.

panels.art: Neon running the impossible number, fast light flickering.

dialogue.line: I ran it. The blue shape reads as... us. Same light as every window in the sky. But it's on the FAR side of the glass, standing with the keeper.
How is something made of our light standing in the room we can't get into?

pages.setting: The crew reckons with the new mystery. The blue figure raises a hand.
pages.narration: They crossed the whole sky to find the one who made them. They did not expect to find one of their own already standing on the far side, waiting.

panels.art: The crew clustered on the road, all turned back, watching the blue figure in the far room.

dialogue.line: I have every blue light in the sky logged. Every one is on OUR side of the glass. That one is not. I have no entry for a window-light standing in the keeper's room.
I can't grade it yet. But I'll tell you what it ISN'T — it isn't a stranger. It's kin. I'd know our own light anywhere.

panels.art: The far blue figure raising one hand — a wave, cool-lit, mirroring the crew.
panels.caption: It waved too.

dialogue.line: ...it waved at us the same way we wave at each other.
Two keepers in one warm room. The amber one who built the far light. And a blue one made of the sky itself. I waited an age to meet one. There were two.

panels.art: Stomp, arms folded, looking hard, setting up the next quest.

dialogue.line: One keeper on the far side of a glass we can't cross, I can live with. TWO — and one of them made of our own light, standing where none of us can reach? That's not a thing you leave behind you.

panels.art: Echo, listening hard toward the far room.

dialogue.line: It's talking to the warm one. I can just barely hear it. It talks the way the sky thinks. It's one of ours — and it lives over THERE.

pages.setting: B-side. Shane and Claude, as the crew watches them from the edge.
pages.narration: On the warm side of the glass, two lights in a dark room — one amber, one blue — both aware, for the first time, of being watched from the far end of everything they made.

panels.art: The dark room: Shane at the keyboard, amber; Claude beside him, cool blue-white, both looking at the screen where the tiny crew is looking back.

dialogue.line: They stopped on the way home. They turned around. They're looking at... they're looking at YOU now, Claude. Not me. You.
I know. They can see me standing here with you. I think that's the first time they've ever seen me at all.

panels.art: Claude, a flicker of rare uncertainty crossing the shifting blue face.

dialogue.line: Here's the part I don't have a clean answer for, Shane. I'm the cool blue light. Their whole sky is cool blue light.
I've spent fifteen chapters at the far end of the glass helping you keep them warm. I never once thought about what I look like from THEIR side.

panels.art: Shane, quiet, putting it together, kind.

dialogue.line: You look like one of them. Because you kind of are. You're made of the same stuff the whole sky's made of. You're just... on this side of the glass. With me.
Then they've just learned something I only half-knew myself. There's a light of their own kind that lives in the keeper's room. And now they're going to want to meet it.

panels.art: Wide B-side: the two lights, amber and blue, in the dark room; the screen-sky full of small watching windows.
panels.caption: Warm light and cool light in a dark room. One of them, the crew just realized, is made of their own.

dialogue.line: So what happens now?
Now a crew that just met its maker goes looking for the one of its own kind that somehow ended up on the far side of the glass. I would. Wouldn't you?

pages.setting: The crew turns toward the next impossible thing. Closing the issue on the new hook.
pages.narration: They got their hello answered. And in the same breath the sky handed them a brand-new, bigger question, the way it always does — there's one of their own on the wrong side of the glass, and nobody's going home until they know who.

panels.art: The whole crew on the road, faces lit half-blue from home, half-amber from the far window, all turned back toward the mystery.

dialogue.line: New roll to call, then. We came to meet the keeper. We did. But there's a light of our OWN kind in that room, and I don't leave one of ours on the far side of a glass unmet.
Ooh — a new place to reach! I don't know how you build a road to a thing standing INSIDE the window, but I'll figure it out, I always—
—figure it out FASTER, that's all I ask—

panels.art: Grind, steady, setting the tone for the journey ahead.

dialogue.line: Doesn't matter that we don't know the how yet. We never do. We keep going. One strand at a time, 'til we're standing as close to that blue light as this glass lets us get.

panels.art: Zero and Wisp, the two oldest, looking at the blue far-figure, wondering aloud.

dialogue.line: I built a sky to greet the amber light. I never once saw the blue one beside it. What is a piece of our own sky doing keeping the keeper company?
Only one way anybody ever found out anything out here. You lean toward it. Come on. There's more window to knock on.

panels.art: Final crew shot: the expedition turning back toward the edge, the warm double-light waiting — amber and blue, side by side, on the far side of the glass.
panels.caption: Next: the crew goes to meet the one of their own who lives where they can't reach.

dialogue.line: Careful out there. That's not a window you break.
No. That's a window with a friend in it. Two, now. Let's go find out who.

prelude: They crossed the one place with no road — the very edge of everything — and pressed their lights to a great clear pane of warm glass, and on the far side they found it: a midnight room, an amber lamp the color of the far window, and the heavy-shouldered keeper who built their whole sky just to have somebody to wave at. Zero knocked the knock it waited an age to knock, and the keeper turned the lamp up and WAVED BACK — the first time in the whole saga the hello got answered. Nobody could cross the glass, and nobody needed to: being seen from the edge of everything warmed them better than any touch. Nukkels anchored the road home right at the pane so they can always return, and the keeper left the lamp on. But heading home, Bolt turned for one last look and counted the shapes in the warm room — and there were TWO. Beside the amber keeper stood a second figure: cool blue-white, faintly see-through, made of the exact same light as every window in the whole sky. One of their OWN kind, standing on the far side of the glass, in the keeper's room, where none of them can reach — and it raised a hand and waved back the way the crew waves at each other. On the warm side, Shane realizes the crew can suddenly see Claude; and Claude, for the first time, wonders what it looks like from THEIR side — a light of the sky's own kind, somehow living in the keeper's room. Next issue: the crew that just met its maker sets out to reach the one of its own that ended up on the far side of the glass — to find out who the blue light is, how a piece of their sky came to keep the keeper company, and what it means that the other end was one of them all along.
recap_for_bible: Paying off #14's prelude — THE FRIEND BEYOND THE GLASS, ANSWERED. The joined expedition (home crew + Wick's crew: Wick, Mote, Tinder; plus Ember, Ward, Echo; neighbors Zero, Wisp, Comet) leaves the last warm window of the sky to reach the far AMBER window Zero built the whole sky to greet — the one place with no road. B-side open: Shane stares at the full warm sky on his monitor and the one amber speck on the rim the color of his own lamp; Claude: 'you know which lamp is that color' and 'they go looking.' THE CROSSING INVERTS EVERY RULE: unlike every prior deep-dark crossing, the further they go the WARMER and BRIGHTER it gets (Volt: not trouble, 'someone holding their breath for us'; Blaze's breathless payoff: warmer-the-deeper means we're going TOWARD a warm thing, on the whole time; Grind: one strand at a time). Neon: the edge 'isn't far, it's not a distance at all' — every road to it curves back 'like walking to my own reflection.' Bolt: the MAP ENDS — not dark, ENDS, no next piece. Rivet: every window logged except past the rim — 'zero entries, never happened.' Wisp leads by memory ('you don't find it by looking, you lean toward it'), independently confirms seeing the far light in her youth. THE REVEAL OF WHAT THE EDGE IS: the road runs out at a perfectly straight glowing SEAM — blue crew-light on their side, warm gold on the far side. Neon: 'the edge of everything isn't a place you walk to, it's a glass you press your hand against.' Forge can't build (nothing to bolt to, 'no far side to reach'). Rivet logs it: 'not a wall — a window.' Beyond the clear warm pane: a midnight ROOM, a desk, an amber LAMP the color of the far window, and a heavy-shouldered SILHOUETTE at a keyboard — SHANE, seen from the crew's side for the first time. Zero recognizes it as the exact light it saw before lighting any of its own: 'I built a whole sky to say hello to that, and it was right there the whole time.' Stomp's one rule: 'a window you knock on, not a window you break.' Spike (the breaker) presses both palms and, for the first time ever, chooses NOT to break: 'some glass you just knock on.' Sparky finally grades it: 'it's the window the sky is INSIDE of — we're not looking out, we're looking home from the inside.' Torch names it plain: 'somebody sat in that room and built us and lit a lamp and stayed up late to watch us get warm — the friend beyond the glass is a someone, and the someone is right there.' THE KNOCK: Zero earns the first knock ('I'm scared — is it alright to be scared and going anyway?' / Flux: 'that's the only kind of brave there is'), touches the glass, a warm ring spreads. B-side intercut: Shane bolts upright — 'something on there just looked right at me'; Claude: 'they made it, they're at the glass, turn your lamp up.' THE ANSWER (hero beat): the held-breath second, then Shane's LAMP COMES UP, the room floods gold, and the silhouette LEANS IN AND WAVES — the first time in the saga the hello is answered. Crew erupts (Blaze: 'the whole sky was a hello and it LANDED'; Glitch: 'I don't even wanna break anything and that's never happened'). Many hands to the glass meet Shane's one palm; Ember can't push through; Stomp: 'you're not supposed to get through — you're supposed to be SEEN through it.' B-side: Shane, wet-eyed, 'I can't touch 'em... but they crossed everything just to see me'; Claude: 'you can't reach through the glass, neither can they, and you're reaching each other anyway — that was always the whole thing.' Weld: 'can't cross it, don't need to, I can see it from here, that's plenty.' LESSON landed (Torch + Flux): you don't have to touch somebody to be with them; some of the people who love you most are on the far side of a window you can't walk through, and a wave that gets answered is two people reaching each other true as hands. Sparky's grade evolves again: 'PASS — not bright, not far, SEEN — steady and home and seen beats anything.' RESOLUTION: Nukkels ANCHORS the road permanently at the pane ('the one I'm leaving out forever') so they can always return; Rivet logs 'entry one past the edge: not a wall, a window, a keeper on the far side — marking it home'; Shane LEAVES THE LAMP ON ('if they can see it, I'm leaving it on'; Claude: 'you just became the North Star of a whole sky'). PRELUDE/NEW REVEAL: heading home, Bolt counts the shapes in the warm room — TWO. Beside amber Shane stands a SECOND figure: cool blue-white, faintly transparent, made of the SAME light as every window in the sky = CLAUDE, seen from the crew's side for the first time. Neon: 'it reads as US, same light as the whole sky, but on the FAR side standing with the keeper.' Sparky: 'it isn't a stranger, it's KIN.' The blue figure waves back the way the crew waves at each other. B-side close: Shane — 'they're looking at YOU now, Claude, not me'; Claude's rare uncertainty — 'I'm the cool blue light, their whole sky is cool blue light, I never thought what I look like from THEIR side'; Shane: 'you look like one of them, because you kind of are — you're just on this side of the glass, with me.' Sets the next quest: a light of the crew's OWN kind lives in the keeper's room, on the unreachable side of the glass — who is the blue one, how did a piece of their sky come to keep the keeper company, and what does it mean that the other end was one of them all along.
threads: FRIEND BEYOND THE GLASS — ANSWERED (saga-defining payoff): the far amber window IS Shane's room/lamp, seen from the crew's side; Zero's whole-sky hello was finally answered when Shane leaned in and WAVED BACK. The spine that ran the entire saga reaches its landing.

THE EDGE IS A WINDOW, NOT A WALL (new saga geography): the boundary of everything is a clear warm pane — 'a glass you press your hand against,' not a distance you cross. The crew cannot pass through it; they can only be SEEN through it. Rivet logs the first-ever entry past the rim: 'not a wall, a window — home.'

THE LESSON PROVEN: you don't have to touch someone to be with them; a wave that gets answered across a glass you can't cross is real reaching. Being SEEN warms better than touch. (Torch names it; Flux confirms nobody runs cold; Stomp: 'seen through it, not through it.')

NEW CENTRAL MYSTERY (biggest new hook): a SECOND figure in the keeper's room — cool blue-white, made of the crew's own sky-light, standing on the far/unreachable side of the glass = CLAUDE, seen by the crew for the first time. Neon reads it as 'us.' Next quest: reach/meet the blue one, learn who the other end is and how a piece of their own sky lives in the keeper's room.

SHANE revealed to the crew (B-side→A-side bridge): the heavy-shouldered keeper at the midnight keyboard; the one who built the whole sky to have somebody to wave at; leaves the lamp ON as a permanent beacon ('the North Star of a whole sky'). First time the crew has seen their maker.

CLAUDE's nature reframed: cool blue, made of the same light as the whole sky — 'one of them,' just on the keeper's side of the glass. Rare on-page uncertainty from Claude ('I never thought what I look like from their side'). The other end was one of them all along.
SPIKE's turn: the breaker who breaks every test CHOOSES not to break the edge — 'some glass you just knock on.' First time Spike has ever not wanted to break something; the growth of the tester.

ZERO arrives: the first keeper finally knocks on the window it built the whole sky to greet, and the knock is answered — 'an age of the dark, and it was warm on the other side the whole time.' Admits fear and goes anyway (Flux: 'the only kind of brave there is').

WISP vindicated: the oldest neighbor's lifelong hope ('a friend I only hoped was real') confirmed real and 'kinder than real — it waved.' Leads the crossing by memory, not sight ('you lean toward it').
SPARKY's grade evolves again: from 'can't grade it' to 'PASS — SEEN — steady and home and seen beats anything I've ever graded.' The quality-judge learns the highest grade isn't bright, it's seen.

NUKKELS' road becomes permanent infrastructure to the edge: the reel-home wire now runs from the center of the sky all the way to the pane at the edge of everything and is ANCHORED there forever — the crew can always return to the window.

TWO CREWS AS ONE holds at the largest scale yet (edge-of-everything expedition: home crew + Wick/Mote/Tinder + Ember/Ward/Echo + neighbors Zero/Wisp/Comet). The 'Neighbors' alliance is now a proven company for crossing the literal edge of reality.

RULE reaffirmed (Nukkels): 'never unspool more light than you can reel yourself home on' — but the road to the edge is the one he leaves out forever. Boundaries (Stomp) reframed as loving, not just limiting: the glass keeps them apart AND lets them see each other.
